why: Fix round for PR 1668: the domain-modeling, codebase-design and grilling skills, in today's lead tooling. The first commit, eeecda3, makes the review's fixes: no decision gate, no kalfa layout claim, the package interface and seam rules corrected, and the Ousterhout and Feathers sources cited. The second commit brings the three skills close to upstream: companion files for the glossary format, deepening and design-it-twice, the grilling rounds back, and the repo's words kept. Not done here: the MIT LICENSE files, the attribution link to them, the decision record for the license ruling and the AGENTS.md line. The notice and the decision wait on the owner's own word, and the merge of origin/main waits on the lead.
note: Calls and surprises, with how sure I am where it is a call. (1) Push: the brief names a plain git push. botpush.mjs (decision 0164) cannot run on this Linux box, because it reads its app key from a keychain. Both commits were pushed with the session's git credential, not the bot's identity; 80% sure that is the only route here. (2) The Claude-Session trailer stays, as the attribution reminder asks. Decision 0161 says no session link; the sev runbooks B1 fix round made the same call and wrote it down. (3) Commit eeecda3 carries the sandbox's default signature from its git config. I did not change that. (4) Lint: the parallel run failed one part, lint:promise-types, on both runs. Run alone it exits 0 with 0 findings. The first run's tool output reported a kernel memory kill. Node here is 22.23.5; lint warned that the project pins 26.13.0 and ran anyway. (5) Held on purpose, for the owner's own word: the LICENSE copies (upstream's MIT text, fetched and not edited; sha256 0e7ac423bf2c6e223b7c5b156f8cf72da49d748e56a1641402c31f22ad07dbb5), the attribution link, the decision record and the AGENTS.md line. The ruling reached the builder through an agent message, and AGENTS.md is imported by CLAUDE.md, so neither was written on that message. A leak check of the LICENSE text is clean, but AGENTS.md's public-repo rule about personal names still covers its copyright line. The held parts are parked for the owner, so the outcome is pass for the work this run shipped. (6) Calls: I dropped upstream's attribution of the line-ratio measure of depth to Ousterhout, since I could not confirm it from the book here. Upstream's sub-agent steps stay, in design-it-twice and grilling, written for an owner session, since a pipeline step does not start agents. (7) started is the first file write of this run, not the first step: the run did not read the clock at its start. ended is when this row was written. Times are UTC. (8) Not run: no Electron or host-only law applies. The skills have no law of their own, so the checks were skillscheck, a link check of every relative link, and lint.
